title: Versal base change is smooth over an affine Noetherian base
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work with $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal F$ be fibred in groupoids on their big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. A category fibred in groupoids assigns a groupoid $\mathcal F(T)$ to each scheme $T$ over the base, with pullback functors and coherent identity and composition isomorphisms. Assume that for every base scheme $T$ and $a,b\in\mathcal F(T)$ the presheaf $T'\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}(a|_{T'},b|_{T'})$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume also that for every diagram of base algebras $A\to B\leftarrow B'$ with $B'\to B$ surjective and square-zero kernel, restriction gives an equivalence $\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_B B'))\simeq\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)\times_{\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B)}\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B')$, where the right side retains the specified isomorphism over $B$ and arrows compatible with it. Assume limit preservation: for every small directed inverse system of affine base schemes with limit $T$, objects over $T$ descend to a stage, isomorphisms between stage objects descend to a sufficiently late common stage, and equality of such isomorphisms over $T$ holds at a sufficiently late common stage. Let $U,V$ be schemes locally of finite type over $S$, with $x\in\mathcal F(U)$ and $y\in\mathcal F(V)$. A point $u\in U$ is of finite type if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-residue-field]. For $x\in\mathcal F(U)$, versality at $u$ means: for every surjection $A'\to A$ of Artinian local base algebras with common residue field identified with $\kappa(u)$ and nilpotent kernel, every map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$, and every $y'\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A')$ with a specified isomorphism $y'|_A\cong x|_A$, there is a lift $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism $y'\cong x|_{A'}$ inducing the specified one. Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize; local means having a unique maximal ideal, and all maps respect the residue-field identifications. The functor sending a scheme $T$ to triples $(a:T\to U,b:T\to V,\alpha:a^*x\cong b^*y)$ is represented by an algebraic space $Z$, with projections $p:Z\to U$ and $q:Z\to V$. If $u_0$ is a finite type point of $U$, $x$ is versal at $u_0$, and $z_0$ is a finite type point of $Z$ over $u_0$, then there is an open subspace $O\subseteq Z$ containing $z_0$ such that $q|_O:O\to V$ is smooth. A finite type point of an algebraic space is a point admitting a closed lift in an etale scheme neighbourhood. Smoothness of spaces is tested on etale scheme charts by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. In particular, let $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ be a first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] with a specified isomorphism $x\cong j^*y$, and let $i:U\to Z$ be the induced map, with $p\circ i=\operatorname{id}_U$ and $q\circ i=j$. Then $i$ sends every finite type point $u_0$ of $U$ to a finite type point $i(u_0)$ of $Z$ over $u_0$; if moreover $x$ is versal at $u_0$, then $q$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $i(u_0)$.

source.place: Tag 0CXM (lemma-base-change-versal), affine Noetherian base case with the limit-preserving parenthetical hypothesis; first-order-thickening section specialization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-limit-preserving-isom-space-lft] to the stated limit-preserving fibred groupoid: its representable Isom spaces give the triples space $Z$ and locally finite type projections, including their composites with etale scheme charts. The scheme $V$ is locally Noetherian: its affine coordinate rings are finitely generated over the given Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Thus [pqf-def-locnoeth] applies. By the definition of a finite type point of $Z$, choose an etale chart $e:W\to Z$ with a closed point $w_0$ mapping to $z_0$, and shrink $W$ to an affine neighbourhood of $w_0$; the point remains closed. Write $r=pe$, $f=qe$, $k=\kappa(u_0)$ and $L=\kappa(w_0)$. Both $r$ and $f$ are locally of finite type. We use the field of the chosen chart point, without identifying it with any field assigned to $z_0$.

The closed point gives a finite type map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to W$ by [lem-trf-closed-point-residue-immersion] and the definition of finite type: on the affine $W$, this is the quotient of its coordinate ring by the maximal ideal of $w_0$, generated as an algebra by the unit. Compose with $r:W\to U$ using [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus]. This composite factors as $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$. Cancellation [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target](a) makes $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally of finite type. Since both spectra have a single point, this says $L$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, and [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] makes $L/k$ finite. Consequently [lem-sfb-artin-pointwise-versal-field-extension] applies to versality at the single point $u_0$ and gives the prescribed-isomorphism lifting property for $x$ at the field-valued point $r(w_0):\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$. The given square-zero gluing condition is exactly the hypothesis in that cited statement; $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, $U/S$ is locally of finite type, and $u_0$ is a finite type point as required. No versality at other points is used.

Test $f:W\to V$ on a small extension $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ with residue field $L$, a map $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to W$ restricting to $w_0$, and a map $b':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to V$ extending $fa$. The triple $ea$ consists of $ra$, $fa$ and $\alpha:(ra)^*x\cong(fa)^*y$. Put $\eta=(b')^*y$. Use the lifting property from [lem-sfb-artin-pointwise-versal-field-extension] with the prescribed isomorphism $\eta|_B\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}}(ra)^*x$. It supplies $c':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to U$ extending $ra$ and $\theta:\eta\cong(c')^*x$ restricting to $\alpha^{-1}$. Therefore $(c',b',\theta^{-1})$ is a $B'$-point $t'$ of the representing space $Z$, restricting exactly to $ea$. The small extension has square-zero kernel by the definition in [lem-sfb-smooth-fixed-residue-artinian-test]. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-space-infinitesimal-lifting] to $e:W\to Z$, $t'$ and $a$; the result is $a':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to W$ with $ea'=t'$ and restriction $a$. Its composite with $f$ is $b'$ by the second component of the triple. Thus all the fixed-residue small-extension tests for $f$ at $w_0$ hold.

source.place: Tag 0CXM proof, fibre-product deformation square; its smoothness argument written directly on triples.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-smooth-fixed-residue-artinian-test], since $V$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ locally of finite type, there is an open $N\subseteq W$ containing $w_0$ with $N\to V$ smooth. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], the image of $N\to Z$ is an open subspace $O$ containing $z_0$, and $N\to O$ is surjective etale. To check $O\to V$ on any etale scheme chart $T\to O$, form $T\times_O N$. It is a scheme because $N\to O$ is representable, by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. It covers $T$ etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its map to $N$ is etale, so its composite to $V$ is smooth, since etale maps are smooth and smooth maps compose [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Smoothness descends to $T\to V$ by [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness]. This proves the required smoothness of $q|_O$ by the chart definition, with no assumption that $Z$ itself is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 0CXM (lemma-base-change-versal), last paragraph; etale descent to the image open.

proof.text: For the specialization, the triple $(\operatorname{id}_U,j,x\cong j^*y)$ defines $i:U\to Z$ with $pi=\operatorname{id}_U$ and $qi=j$. The identity of $U$ is locally of finite type, so [lem-sfb-space-lft-cancellation], applied to $i$ followed by $p$, makes $i$ locally of finite type. For every finite type point $u_0$, the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u_0)\to U$ is of finite type by hypothesis; composing it with $i$ is locally of finite type by [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus]. Hence [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-point-characterization] makes $i(u_0)$ a finite type point of $Z$ in exactly the closed-chart sense used in the statement. It lies over $u_0$ because $pi=\operatorname{id}_U$. If $x$ is versal there, apply the already proved assertion to $z_0=i(u_0)$. This yields the claimed smooth open neighbourhood. This point argument works for every compatible section triple, hence for the stated first-order thickening.
